layers.name: Data & Knowledge
layers.description: The information the AI can use: documents, databases, retrieval, context, memory and the systems that keep that information current.

layers.name: Model
layers.description: The model that performs language, reasoning, coding, vision or audio tasks. This is the raw capability layer.

layers.name: Agent & Infrastructure
layers.description: The runtime around the model: tools, state, memory, orchestration, permissions, sandboxes and the ability to take actions.

layers.name: Application & Workflow
layers.description: The user experience and business process where AI is used, from copilots to end-to-end task flows.

layers.name: Production & Business
layers.description: Everything needed to run AI responsibly at scale: evals, monitoring, governance, cost, risk, reliability and measurable business value.

primitives.name: Compute
primitives.description: Where it runs. This covers model inference, agent runtimes, application code, indexing, evals and other processing.

primitives.name: Networking
primitives.description: How it connects. This covers traffic between users, models, tools, data sources, APIs and enterprise systems.

primitives.name: Storage
primitives.description: Where data and state live. This includes documents, databases, vectors, memory, logs, traces and application state.

primitives.name: Security
primitives.description: Who or what is allowed access. This includes identity, permissions, secrets, isolation, approvals and audit controls.

impacts.name: Disruptive
impacts.description: Changes what is practical to build or reshapes the market enough that old assumptions need to be reconsidered.

impacts.name: Step-change
impacts.description: A clear jump in capability, cost, reliability or usability that changes architecture decisions, but does not reset the whole market.

impacts.name: Incremental
impacts.description: A meaningful improvement to an existing approach. It matters, but the basic architecture and workflow stay mostly the same.

impacts.name: Packaging / distribution
impacts.description: The underlying capability mostly existed already, but it becomes easier, cheaper, more integrated or available to more teams.

trajectories.description: Getting the right information into the system.
trajectories.now: Long context, retrieval, connected company data, citations, and memory are increasingly combined.
trajectories.direction: Permission-aware organizational context that stays fresh and can be reused across models and agents.
trajectories.constraint: Freshness, provenance, permissions, data quality, and cost.

trajectories.now: Frontier models reason longer, operate computers, work across modalities, and improve rapidly on professional tasks.
trajectories.direction: Broader, more general capability with adaptive reasoning and model routing by task, cost, latency, and risk.
trajectories.constraint: Alignment, inference cost, reliability, misuse risk, and knowing when capability is actually trustworthy.

trajectories.description: Turning model capability into sustained action.
trajectories.now: Managed runtimes, tools, MCP, subagents, computer use, state, and tracing support longer tasks.
trajectories.direction: Persistent software actors that can work for hours or days, recover from failure, coordinate, and operate across systems.
trajectories.constraint: Long-horizon reliability, identity, bounded permissions, verification, and recovery.

trajectories.description: Where AI changes how work is actually done.
trajectories.now: The pattern is moving from assistance beside the workflow to agents executing meaningful parts of the workflow.
trajectories.direction: AI-native processes where machines execute routine and analytical work while people handle goals, judgment, approvals, and exceptions.
trajectories.constraint: Workflow redesign, adoption, accountability, process ownership, and proving business value.

trajectories.description: Making AI controllable, measurable, and economically useful.
trajectories.now: Evals, traces, trajectory monitoring, governance, approval gates, and cost controls are becoming core production architecture.
trajectories.direction: Continuous risk-based control where capability, alignment, reliability, cost, and business value are measured together.
trajectories.constraint: Scalable alignment and oversight as models become more capable and autonomous.

updates.title: ChatGPT put conversational generative AI in a public product
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a public research preview built around a conversational interface with follow-up dialogue.
updates.whyCare: It gave a broad audience a simple way to use a capable language model and made natural-language interaction a mainstream product pattern.
updates.before: Foundation models were mainly experienced through research demos, APIs and specialist tools.
updates.after: A general-purpose conversational interface became a practical product surface for everyday users and teams.
updates.learn: Treat natural language as an interface layer, while separating the chat experience from the underlying model and business workflow.
updates.architectureImplication: Treat natural language as an interface layer, while separating the chat experience from the underlying model and business workflow.

updates.title: GPT-4 raised the capability ceiling and added image input
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-4 as a large multimodal model that accepted image and text inputs and improved performance across professional and academic benchmarks.
updates.whyCare: More capable models made higher-value knowledge work and multimodal applications more credible, while also increasing the need for evaluation and control.
updates.before: Most mainstream GenAI applications were built around weaker text-first models.
updates.after: Architects could consider more complex reasoning, higher-stakes workflows and image-plus-text use cases.
updates.learn: Model capability matters, but architecture still needs evals, data, controls and workflow design around it.
updates.architectureImplication: Model capability matters, but architecture still needs evals, data, controls and workflow design around it.

updates.title: Function calling made model-to-tool connections more structured
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI added function calling so models could choose a described function and return structured arguments that software could use to call APIs or tools.
updates.whyCare: This moved applications beyond free-form text toward systems where models could reliably trigger software actions.
updates.before: Developers often parsed model text or built brittle prompt conventions to connect models to software.
updates.after: Models could return structured tool calls that application code could validate and execute.
updates.learn: Separate model judgment from deterministic execution. Validate arguments and permissions before tools run.

sources.name: OpenAI - Function calling and other API updates

updates.architectureImplication: Separate model judgment from deterministic execution. Validate arguments and permissions before tools run.

updates.title: Gemini 1.5 pushed long context to one million tokens in preview
updates.whatChanged: Google introduced Gemini 1.5 Pro with a standard 128,000-token context and a one-million-token experimental context window for selected users.
updates.whyCare: Very long context changed the trade-off between retrieval, chunking and putting large amounts of source material directly into model context.
updates.before: Large document collections usually had to be aggressively chunked and retrieved in small pieces.
updates.after: Some workloads could send much larger corpora directly, while retrieval remained important for cost, freshness, permissions and precision.
updates.learn: Choose between long context, retrieval and hybrids based on data size, freshness, latency, cost and access control.
updates.architectureImplication: Choose between long context, retrieval and hybrids based on data size, freshness, latency, cost and access control.

updates.title: GPT-4o integrated text, vision and audio with much lower interaction latency
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced GPT-4o as a model designed to reason across text, audio and vision in real time, including much faster audio interaction.
updates.whyCare: Integrated multimodality reduced the need to stitch together separate speech, vision and language components for some experiences.
updates.before: Voice and multimodal applications often required several models and conversion stages.
updates.after: A single model family could handle more of the interaction loop directly.
updates.learn: For multimodal systems, architecture decisions shift toward streaming, latency, session state, interruption handling and cost.
updates.architectureImplication: For multimodal systems, architecture decisions shift toward streaming, latency, session state, interruption handling and cost.

updates.title: Llama 3.1 expanded the credible open-model option
updates.whatChanged: Meta released Llama 3.1, including a 405B model with 128K context and weights available for broad use under its license.
updates.whyCare: The gap between closed frontier APIs and models teams could run or control themselves narrowed for more use cases.
updates.before: Frontier-level capability was concentrated more heavily in closed hosted APIs.
updates.after: Enterprises had a stronger open-model option for control, customization and deployment choices.
updates.learn: Model selection should include deployment control, licensing, data location, cost, skill requirements and operational burden.
updates.architectureImplication: Model selection should include deployment control, licensing, data location, cost, skill requirements and operational burden.

updates.title: o1 made test-time reasoning a visible model design choice
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released o1-preview, a model series designed to spend more time reasoning before responding and to improve on harder science, coding and math tasks.
updates.whyCare: It made inference-time reasoning effort an explicit trade-off between capability, latency and cost.
updates.before: Most model calls were treated as roughly the same kind of single-pass generation.
updates.after: Architects could choose when a task justified more reasoning time and cost.
updates.learn: Route work by difficulty and value. Not every task needs expensive reasoning.
updates.architectureImplication: Route work by difficulty and value. Not every task needs expensive reasoning.

updates.title: Computer use let a frontier model operate graphical software
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released computer use in public beta so Claude could inspect screens, move a cursor, click and type through software interfaces.
updates.whyCare: Agents could act in systems that had no clean API or purpose-built integration, although reliability and security remained difficult.
updates.before: Automation generally needed APIs, scripts or brittle browser automation.
updates.after: A model could interact with existing graphical software in a more general way.
updates.learn: Computer use expands reach but raises verification, sandboxing, credential and recovery requirements.

sources.name: Anthropic - Developing a computer use model

updates.architectureImplication: Computer use expands reach but raises verification, sandboxing, credential and recovery requirements.

updates.title: MCP introduced an open standard for connecting AI systems to tools and data
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol as a standard way to connect AI assistants to data sources, business tools and development environments.
updates.whyCare: It created a common integration pattern where each model application did not need a completely bespoke connector for every source.
updates.before: Tool and data connections were commonly implemented separately for each application or framework.
updates.after: A shared protocol could let tools and data sources expose reusable interfaces to many AI clients.
updates.learn: Watch standards adoption. Protocols matter when ecosystems converge around them, not just when they are announced.

sources.name: Anthropic - Introducing the Model Context Protocol

updates.architectureImplication: Watch standards adoption. Protocols matter when ecosystems converge around them, not just when they are announced.

updates.title: DeepSeek-R1 increased pressure on reasoning cost and open access
updates.whatChanged: DeepSeek released R1 and distilled reasoning models with open weights under the MIT license and published low API pricing.
updates.whyCare: Reasoning capability became available through a wider range of deployment and cost options, increasing pressure on closed-model economics.
updates.before: Advanced reasoning was more strongly associated with a small number of closed providers.
updates.after: Teams had more options to trade off model quality, hosting control, openness and cost.
updates.learn: Avoid hard-wiring architecture to one provider. Model routing and portability become more valuable as capability and price move quickly.
updates.architectureImplication: Avoid hard-wiring architecture to one provider. Model routing and portability become more valuable as capability and price move quickly.

updates.title: Agent building blocks moved further into managed platform infrastructure
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released the Responses API, built-in tools and an Agents SDK with tracing for building agentic applications.
updates.whyCare: Core agent runtime capabilities became easier to consume as managed services, reducing custom orchestration work for teams using that stack.
updates.before: Teams commonly assembled tool use, orchestration, tracing and state through custom code or separate frameworks.
updates.after: More of the agent harness could be bought as platform infrastructure.
updates.learn: Distinguish fundamental capability changes from packaging changes. Managed runtimes can still matter because they change build-versus-buy economics.

sources.name: OpenAI - New tools for building agents

updates.architectureImplication: Distinguish fundamental capability changes from packaging changes. Managed runtimes can still matter because they change build-versus-buy economics.

updates.title: A2A formalized a direction toward agent-to-agent interoperability
updates.whatChanged: Google announced the Agent2Agent protocol to let agents built by different vendors or frameworks communicate and coordinate.
updates.whyCare: It made cross-agent interoperability a clearer ecosystem goal, although standards need adoption before they become architecture defaults.
updates.before: Multi-agent systems usually assumed one framework, one vendor or custom communication conventions.
updates.after: A shared protocol could reduce coupling between agent systems if ecosystem adoption follows.
updates.learn: Treat emerging protocols as directional signals first. Adopt them when ecosystem support and customer requirements justify it.
updates.architectureImplication: Treat emerging protocols as directional signals first. Adopt them when ecosystem support and customer requirements justify it.

updates.title: Managed agent runtimes added remote MCP and more reliable long-running execution
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI added remote MCP support, background mode and additional reliability and privacy features to its Responses API.
updates.whyCare: Agent infrastructure started absorbing more connectivity, long-running execution and observability concerns into managed runtimes.
updates.before: Teams had to assemble more of the connectivity and long-running execution behavior themselves.
updates.after: Managed platforms covered more of the operational agent harness.
updates.learn: Compare managed convenience with portability, visibility, security requirements and provider lock-in.

sources.name: OpenAI - New tools and features in the Responses API

updates.architectureImplication: Compare managed convenience with portability, visibility, security requirements and provider lock-in.

updates.title: Long-running agent reliability is becoming the real bottleneck
updates.whatChanged: Frontier agent systems can already execute multi-step work, but reliability falls as tasks get longer and tool use becomes more complex. The engineering focus is shifting toward state, recovery, verification and trajectory-level control.
updates.whyCare: For enterprise architecture, the question is moving from whether an agent can do one task to whether it can complete a long workflow safely and repeatedly.
updates.before: Agents were judged mainly on impressive individual tasks and demos.
updates.after: Architecture increasingly centers on reliable execution across many steps, tools, failures and approvals.
updates.learn: Long-horizon reliability, persistent state, retries, recovery, verification and human escalation.
updates.architectureImplication: Long-horizon reliability, persistent state, retries, recovery, verification and human escalation.

updates.title: Agent security is moving from app security to actor-level control
updates.whatChanged: As agents gain tools and autonomy, enterprises increasingly need agent identity, scoped permissions, sandboxing, audit logs and approval gates.
updates.whyCare: An agent with access to enterprise systems behaves more like a software actor than a chatbot. It needs its own operating controls.
updates.before: Secure the AI application and its API access.
updates.after: Secure each agent as an actor with identity, privileges and auditable actions.
updates.learn: Least privilege, credential isolation, agent identity, sandboxing and approval gates.
updates.architectureImplication: Least privilege, credential isolation, agent identity, sandboxing and approval gates.

updates.title: Managed agent runtimes continue to reduce custom harness work
updates.whatChanged: More providers are packaging context, tools, subagents, execution and long-running task infrastructure into managed agent runtimes.
updates.whyCare: The underlying patterns already existed, but lower implementation friction changes build-versus-buy decisions.
updates.before: Teams assembled much of the harness themselves or through separate frameworks.
updates.after: More runtime pieces can be consumed as managed infrastructure.
updates.learn: Agent harness means state, context, tools, execution, retries, permissions, memory and observability.
updates.architectureImplication: Agent harness means state, context, tools, execution, retries, permissions, memory and observability.

updates.title: Agent evaluation is expanding from output quality to behaviour
updates.whatChanged: Teams increasingly need to inspect which tools an agent used, which path it took and whether it stayed inside policy, not only whether the final answer looked correct.
updates.whyCare: A correct-looking output can still come from an unsafe or invalid path. That matters once agents can take actions.
updates.before: Evaluate whether the final answer is correct.
updates.after: Evaluate both the result and the action trajectory that produced it.
updates.learn: Output evals, trajectory evals, audit logs, policy checks and risk-based human review.
updates.architectureImplication: Output evals, trajectory evals, audit logs, policy checks and risk-based human review.

updates.title: Enterprise agent building, governance, and scale became a single platform concern
updates.whatChanged: Google Cloud Next 2026 introduced an end-to-end enterprise agent platform spanning agent building, governance, and scale.
updates.whyCare: Agent infrastructure is becoming a first-class cloud platform category rather than a collection of disconnected components.
updates.before: Teams stitched together models, tools, orchestration, identity, and governance across separate services.
updates.after: Cloud platforms increasingly package those concerns into integrated agent platforms.
updates.learn: Compare integrated agent platforms on portability, observability, governance, cost, and ecosystem fit.
updates.architectureImplication: Compare integrated agent platforms on portability, observability, governance, cost, and ecosystem fit.

updates.title: Persistent agents moved deeper into everyday workplace software
updates.whatChanged: Google announced Gemini Spark as a persistent personal AI agent designed to act across Workspace applications under user direction.
updates.whyCare: It shows the application layer moving from a chat tool beside work toward a persistent actor inside the software people already use.
updates.before: AI mainly helped inside isolated prompts or single application features.
updates.after: A persistent agent can coordinate work across multiple everyday applications.
updates.learn: Workflow architecture needs clear delegation, approvals, context boundaries, and user control.
updates.architectureImplication: Workflow architecture needs clear delegation, approvals, context boundaries, and user control.

updates.title: Claude Fable 5 raised the bar for long, complex knowledge and coding work
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released Fable 5 with stronger performance on longer and more complex tasks across coding, knowledge work, vision, and research.
updates.whyCare: Long-horizon model capability is becoming a core differentiator, not only benchmark accuracy on short tasks.
updates.before: Hard tasks often required users to break work into many smaller supervised steps.
updates.after: Stronger models can sustain larger projects and longer reasoning chains before handing control back.
updates.learn: Evaluate models on the duration and complexity of work they can complete reliably, not only benchmark scores.
updates.architectureImplication: Evaluate models on the duration and complexity of work they can complete reliably, not only benchmark scores.

updates.title: Long-running models forced safety evaluation to move from actions to trajectories
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI reported novel failures during limited internal use of a long-running model and responded with new evaluations, long-horizon alignment work, trajectory monitoring, and more user control.
updates.whyCare: Once systems persist and act over time, checking isolated outputs is not enough.
updates.before: Safety and evaluation could focus mainly on individual model responses or bounded tasks.
updates.after: Production control increasingly needs to evaluate sequences of actions and intervene across a whole trajectory.
updates.learn: Learn trajectory-level monitoring, long-horizon evals, approval boundaries, and recovery.

sources.name: OpenAI - Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models

updates.architectureImplication: Learn trajectory-level monitoring, long-horizon evals, approval boundaries, and recovery.

updates.title: Enterprise AI is moving from assistance toward execution inside real workflows
updates.whatChanged: Published enterprise examples increasingly show agents connected to tools and company context for onboarding, account management, developer work, and other multi-step processes.
updates.whyCare: The important application shift is not a better chatbot. It is delegation of substantive parts of a business process.
updates.before: AI mostly assisted people with drafting, search, and isolated tasks beside the workflow.
updates.after: Leading teams increasingly connect agents to context and tools and make successful workflows repeatable.
updates.learn: Start workflow design with task boundaries, data, tools, approvals, failure handling, and measurable outcome.
updates.architectureImplication: Start workflow design with task boundaries, data, tools, approvals, failure handling, and measurable outcome.

updates.title: Frontier models pushed further into computer use, science, cyber, and professional work
updates.whatChanged: A new frontier generation improved across computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work.
updates.whyCare: Frontier capability is increasingly crossing from answering questions into operating software and carrying out complex professional tasks.
updates.before: Models were less reliable across long, tool-using professional work and advanced computer use.
updates.after: A frontier model can handle a broader set of complex tasks and operate software more effectively.
updates.learn: As capability broadens, architecture must pair models with stronger controls, routing, monitoring, and risk assessment.
updates.architectureImplication: As capability broadens, architecture must pair models with stronger controls, routing, monitoring, and risk assessment.

updates.title: Automated research moved from aspiration to an internal working milestone
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI said coding agents were accelerating internal research and that it had reached its goal of an automated research intern working under human supervision.
updates.whyCare: Automating parts of AI research itself is a directional signal toward agents that improve the speed of capability and alignment research.
updates.before: AI systems mainly assisted researchers on bounded tasks.
updates.after: Research agents can take on larger experiment and implementation loops under supervision.
updates.learn: Watch research automation because it can accelerate both model progress and the need for alignment and governance.
updates.architectureImplication: Watch research automation because it can accelerate both model progress and the need for alignment and governance.

updates.title: Business data, analysis, dashboards, and action are converging into one agent workflow
updates.whatChanged: A business data agent combined connected company data, investigation, analysis, and interactive dashboards in one workflow.
updates.whyCare: It packages retrieval, business context, analysis, and reporting into a simpler experience for non-specialists.
updates.before: Business users often waited for analysts or moved manually between BI tools, SQL, spreadsheets, and reports.
updates.after: A conversational agent can investigate connected business data and create shareable analysis directly.
updates.learn: The architectural issues move to data permissions, metric definitions, provenance, freshness, and auditability.

sources.name: OpenAI - Now everyone can put data to work

updates.architectureImplication: The architectural issues move to data permissions, metric definitions, provenance, freshness, and auditability.

updates.title: Vertical AI products are combining trusted data, reasoning, and templates into complete workflows
updates.whatChanged: A financial-services AI product combined premium data, reasoning, citations, and firm templates for research, models, and client materials.
updates.whyCare: It shows the application layer becoming more domain-specific and workflow-complete rather than offering a generic assistant alone.
updates.before: Teams assembled generic AI, data subscriptions, templates, and controls separately.
updates.after: A vertical product can package trusted data, domain workflows, output formats, and governance together.
updates.learn: Expect more industry-specific AI products where data rights, workflow design, and governance matter as much as the model.
updates.architectureImplication: Expect more industry-specific AI products where data rights, workflow design, and governance matter as much as the model.

updates.title: AI use is beginning to expand the set of tasks people regularly perform
updates.whatChanged: Economic research reported that some AI-assisted tasks outside a worker's usual occupation become recurring parts of their workflow.
updates.whyCare: This is an early sign that AI may change job scope and task boundaries, not only make existing tasks faster.
updates.before: AI adoption was often measured as faster execution of the same tasks.
updates.after: Some workers are adding new recurring tasks to their role because AI lowers the expertise or effort barrier.
updates.learn: Measure workflow change, task expansion, and role redesign alongside simple time savings.

sources.name: OpenAI - How workers are unlocking new ways of working

updates.architectureImplication: Measure workflow change, task expansion, and role redesign alongside simple time savings.

updates.title: LLMOps emerged as a distinct production discipline for generative AI
updates.whatChanged: Enterprise guidance began treating LLM applications as systems needing dedicated evaluation, deployment, monitoring, feedback, privacy, and operational management across their lifecycle.
updates.whyCare: Generative AI production work was no longer only conventional software operations. Teams needed practices for non-deterministic outputs, prompts, retrieval, model versions, quality, and safety.
updates.before: Early GenAI work focused heavily on prompts, prototypes, and model capability.
updates.after: Production architecture increasingly included evaluation, validation, monitoring, feedback loops, privacy, and lifecycle management.
updates.learn: A GenAI system needs an operating lifecycle, not only a model endpoint.
updates.architectureImplication: Design evaluation, versioning, monitoring, feedback, and rollback into the system before production rather than adding them after launch.

updates.title: GenAIOps expanded production monitoring beyond infrastructure health
updates.whatChanged: Cloud architecture guidance formalized continuous monitoring of prompts, completions, relevance, safety, data drift, model performance, and workload metrics for GenAI systems.
updates.whyCare: A healthy server does not mean a healthy AI application. Quality, safety, relevance, and model behavior also need production observability.
updates.before: Operations could focus primarily on infrastructure availability, latency, and errors.
updates.after: Production monitoring increasingly covered both system health and AI behavior.
updates.learn: Observe the application, data, model behavior, safety, and infrastructure together.
updates.architectureImplication: Add AI quality and safety telemetry alongside normal application monitoring, with explicit quality gates and auditability.

sources.name: Microsoft Azure Well-Architected - MLOps and GenAIOps

updates.title: Agent runtimes are becoming more elastic for long-running and bursty agents
updates.whatChanged: AWS introduced AgentCore Runtime V2 with memory reclamation during sessions and snapshot-based startup. AWS measured about 2-second P75 cold starts across container images from 200 MB to 2 GB, versus roughly 5.4 to 30 seconds for the earlier runtime.
updates.whyCare: Production agents increasingly need isolated compute that can sit idle, resume quickly, run for long periods, and avoid paying for peak memory throughout a session.
updates.before: Teams often kept agent environments warm, paid for memory held at the session high-water mark, or built their own lifecycle machinery to reduce cold starts and idle cost.
updates.after: A managed agent runtime can scale to zero, reclaim unused memory during a session, and restore prepared environments from snapshots with more predictable startup.
updates.learn: Separate the agent harness from the agent runtime. The harness manages reasoning, tools and context; the runtime provides compute, isolation, state and lifecycle.
updates.architectureImplication: Treat agent execution as its own infrastructure layer and compare managed runtimes on isolation, startup latency, session lifecycle, state, identity, portability and cost.

updates.title: Inference-aware routing is becoming a managed production primitive
updates.whatChanged: AWS introduced SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway, which routes LLM requests using signals such as KV-cache utilization, queue depth, LoRA adapter residency, prefix-cache hit rate and running requests. AWS reports up to 82% lower time-to-first-token in its tests.
updates.whyCare: LLM replicas are not interchangeable in the way ordinary stateless web servers are. Cache state, queues and loaded adapters can materially change latency and GPU efficiency.
updates.before: Generic round-robin or least-connections routing could send a request to a model pod with a poor cache state, a deep queue or the wrong adapter loaded.
updates.after: An inference-aware router can select a backend using model-serving state, improving cache reuse, latency and GPU utilization without changing application clients.
updates.learn: Understand KV cache, prefix caching, time-to-first-token, prefill versus decode, LoRA adapters and inference-aware routing. These increasingly determine self-hosted model economics.
updates.architectureImplication: For dedicated GPU inference, treat routing and cache topology as part of model-serving architecture rather than using a generic load balancer by default.

sources.name: AWS - Introducing SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway

overallDirection.title: From assistants to agents and automated knowledge work
overallDirection.summary: The broad direction is toward systems that reason longer, use tools, act across software, and take on larger portions of real work. Model capability still matters, but the architectural bottleneck is moving toward reliable autonomy and integration.
overallDirection.destination: Increasingly general AI systems that can perform broad cognitive work, research, and operations under human direction. This is a direction of travel, not a guaranteed end state.
overallDirection.constraint: Alignment, monitoring, permissions, security, reliability, and preserving meaningful human control as systems become more autonomous.
